posts.title: The Demons of Volinn, Part 2: Combat, Crawls, and Carryingequipment
posts.description: This is my second post about The Demons of Volinn , a new and in-progress game I started for Minimalist Jam V! Part 1 is here . Equipment # All of the things I want to talk about are a bit intertwined. We’ll start here because it makes the most sense. (Obviously there’s going to be other stuff than what I’m mentioning, but much of it’s kind of self-explanatory and works on a “it does what it says it does” basis - I’m not gonna wax poetic on, like, rope - or it’s something I’m gonna talk about when I get into the setting.) Inventory is slot-based, as you do. You can hold 10 slots, or if your Might is higher than 10, that many slots. It counts what you’re wearing and carrying as well as stuff in your pack. Most stuff is 1, bulky stuff is 2, slight stuff doesn’t count. None of this should probably blow your mind if you’ve read anything in the lineage of the game. posts.title: The Demons of Volinn, Part 1: Inspirations, Tendencies, Weird Little Guys
posts.description: What if I actually told people about the 19,000 word game that I dropped a week ago? Would that be cool or what? Going into Minimalist Jam, I was floating a few ideas as to what to do, and had even outlined one. Then this idea hit me like a bullet and that was that, we were off to the races. So let’s actually talk about it now that I’ve caught my breath a bit. I tend to come to game ideas from odd angles, and this one was no exception. Something had gotten me thinking about Demon’s Souls again, which isn’t uncommon (it’s probably the best one in the series, after all, depending what you want out of them 1 ). This time, though, I had been thinking about two things I don’t regularly think too hard about with it, because I think they’re fairly undercooked: World and Character Tendency, two things more or less unique to that entry that were dropped like a hot rock almost immediately in the rest of the series. posts.title: Post-APOCALYPSE #2: The Death of Tags
posts.description: At the end of the first post in this (intermittent, barely-started) series, I mentioned I wanted to talk about weapons (or specifically armaments), systems, and enemies. All of them changed in the same way: I got rid of tags. The initial approach # This is how I was using tags, initially. For as much as I’ve fully turned around on them, the tags in LIGHT were actually a thing that drew me to the system! So I took that idea and just ran with it as far as I could. Armaments and Enemies # An armament in APOCALYPSE FRAME looks like the following: Sniper Rifle: 2 dice, 3 Harm, Far, Stationary Carbine: 3 dice, 2 Harm, Close/Near, Burst, Mobile Plasma Blade: 1 die, 5 Harm, Close, Energy, Piercing, Charge Which is to say, it’s a combination of: Dice rolled. (See the previous post re: rolling dice.) Harm dealt. (This is the point of most attacks.) Range. (Close is in the same hex 1 , Near is one hex away, Far is two away, Extreme is three.)
